articles.title: McDonald's earnings beat, but traffic to chain's U.S. restaurants falls
articles.summary: At the company's investor day in September, executives said that same-store sales in July and August were slightly negative but they expected September to return to same-store sales growth. Shares of the company rose more than 2% in premarket trading. McDonald's international developmental licensed markets business, which includes Japan and China, reported same-store sales growth of 4.2%.

articles.title: SpaceX, Tesla fall over 4% on Democrats' big win; AI stocks mixed
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence stocks came under pressure overnight as Democrats — seen as proponents of data center moratoriums — won big in midterm elections in key data center hubs. He added that the election in Texas was the "biggest worry" of the night for tech investors and the AI trade because that's where around 25%-30% of data center gigawatts and capacity will come from.

articles.title: Euro zone inflation hits 4% for first time in three years as interest rate hike looms
articles.summary: All euro zone countries saw inflation hold above the European Central Bank's 2% target. The European Central Bank kept its key interest rate at 2.5% last month, following a hike of 25 basis points in September. Robert Mertens, global capital markets senior analyst at Validus Risk Management, cautioned that "ongoing turmoil in the French bond market is placing constraints on ECB policy" and the bank's capacity to get inflation under control.

articles.title: Novo shares jump as Wegovy pill sales impress, drugmaker hikes outlook
articles.summary: Novo posted quarterly earnings ahead of expectations early Wednesday as sales of its Wegovy pill blew past estimates amid continued GLP-1 volume growth globally, sending shares up as much as 6% in early trading. The company updated its outlook to now see adjusted revenue and operating profit growth between negative 2% and 2% at constant exchange rates. The stock fell nearly 8% in one session in September after Novo failed to reassure investors with its post-Wegovy growth strategy.

articles.title: Treasury yields fall as investors crowd into bonds for safety amid election stock sell-off
articles.summary: Treasury yields moved lower on Wednesday as investors sought shelter from a sell-off in equity futures sparked by potential big victories from Democrats in the U.S. The 30-year bond yield slid 3 basis points to 5.29%, and the shorter-term 2-year note yield was broadly flat at 4.6101%. AI-related shares, which have led the bull market, paced the overnight decline on fears that Democrats would slow the data center buildout.

articles.title: Jim Cramer sees signs of life in tech stocks — but not from the usual winners
articles.summary: CNBC's Jim Cramer said Tuesday that a new group of technology stocks may be emerging as market leaders. That was evident during Tuesday's session as gains from Broadcom and Micron supported the major averages — a sign that investors may be shifting toward a different set of tech winners.

articles.title: AMD stock jumps 8% on earnings as data center revenue nearly doubles
articles.summary: CEO Lisa Su said on the earnings call that she expects server revenue to double year over year in 2027 and data center AI growth to accelerate even faster than the company had projected 90 days ago. After years spent chasing Nvidia in the market for artificial intelligence graphics processing units, or GPUs, AMD's central processing units, or CPUs, are experiencing a major resurgence with the rise of agentic AI apps like Meta's Muse.

articles.title: Eaton's strong quarter should mark a bottom for shares of the AI buildout winner
articles.summary: Eaton delivered an excellent quarter on Tuesday, giving shares of the artificial intelligence buildout winner a much-needed jolt. The results and outlook demonstrated why we've stuck with the stock despite a turbulent period for the AI trade. Bottom line The electrical equipment supplier turned in a very strong quarter that should help solidify a bottom in the stock — assuming we don't see a renewed, broad-based rejection of the AI trade.

articles.title: AMD has been crushed into earnings. Here’s one way to trade it
articles.summary: The stock has been caught in the swings of the AI debate all year, but this most recent leg lower was triggered by a wave of disappointing tech earnings. AMD's stock reactions have been mixed in recent quarters, sensitive to guidance and high investor expectations. That may make direction hard to call, but options let investors build a trade that doesn't have to pick a side.

articles.title: JetBlue raises bag fees for third time in a year as fuel costs bite
articles.summary: JetBlue Airways has raised the price of checking a bag for many customers for the third time in less than a year as high fuel costs continue to eat into the industry's profits. Checking a first bag for travelers booked in economy will now be $50, up from $45, if purchased more than 24 hours before departure during a non-peak travel period. If it's paid within 24 hours of departure, the fee will be $60.

articles.title: Election Day: Here is the No. 1 issue we're watching as a signal for stocks
articles.summary: The rotation back into chip stocks comes after Apple shares fell about 2% after providing a disappointing gross margin outlook due to the rising cost of memory chips, which are made by Micron . The recent trend has been for bond prices to rally in a flight to safety when AI stocks sell off. With chip stocks and other AI names rebounding, we're seeing the reverse, with bond prices falling and yields rising.

articles.title: Options traders are betting heavily on these stocks ahead of election results
articles.summary: With prediction markets pricing in a big victory for Democrats in Tuesday's midterm elections, traders are leaning into a group of stocks that investors often categorize as beneficiaries of left-wing leadership. Options trading in clean-energy stocks, particularly solar companies, surged on Tuesday, despite a five-month sell-off in the group that's left most of the companies in the industry group down on the year.

articles.title: Job openings posted big September gain in positive sign for labor market ahead of payrolls report
articles.summary: Openings rose in manufacturing (54,000) as well as state and local government (108,000) and professional and business services (106,000). articles.title: Ferrari raises 2026 guidance after Q3 earnings beat
articles.summary: Ferrari said Tuesday that the guidance improvements were a result of stronger-than-expected customer personalizations, lower than anticipated currency headwinds and a second place finish in the Formula 1 championship. articles.title: Meta seeks to raise up to $25 billion in debt sale as AI spending jumps
articles.summary: Meta is seeking to raise between $20 billion and $25 billion in a bond sale on Tuesday as the company ramps up its spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure along with AI models and services. Final pricing for the bond sale should come Tuesday afternoon, the sources said. Meta previously raised $25 billion in an April bond sale, and said last week that it plans to raise $95 billion in an effort to fund its AI initiatives.

articles.title: Shopify falls 7% after Q3 revenue and merchandise volume miss estimates
articles.summary: Shares of e-commerce platform Shopify fell 7% on Tuesday after the company missed estimates on subscription gross profit and gross merchandise volume. Shopify said it sees revenue growth in the "low thirties" range year over year for the fourth quarter, versus LSEG estimates of 32.1%.

articles.title: Bill Ackman warns of 'casino' stock market as speculative trading grows
articles.summary: "Every number of days, I feel like markets are broken," Ackman said on CNBC's "Squawk Box." "Stocks trade at prices that make no sense to me. "I don't think that's inherently good for the economy, for society, and it's leading to these massive moves in stocks." The founder of Pershing Square Capital Management said those same dislocations in the market have given the hedge fund the opportunity to snag big bargains.
